# SK1020 — Use `ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull`

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

A hand-written null guard that `ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull` already is.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Modernization |
| Default severity | suggestion |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | yes, safe |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 0.6 |
| ReSharper | `UseThrowIfNullMethod` (`resharper_use_throw_if_null_method_highlighting`) |

## Why

The BCL helper is one line instead of three, captures the argument expression itself through `CallerArgumentExpression` so the message cannot drift from the parameter name, and is annotated so the nullable analysis knows the argument is non-null afterwards — which the hand-written form only manages when the `throw` is the whole `if` body.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
if (source is null) {
    throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(source));
}
```

Write:

```csharp
ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(source);
```

## The ReSharper mapping

⚠ The export sets `resharper_use_throw_if_null_method_highlighting = none`, so reading the key as authoritative would switch this rule off in the repository Skala was built for. That measurement is why --resharper-severities is opt-in. docs/plan/16 § Q5.

## When it does not fire

Requires `System.ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull` to exist in the compilation, so a project on an older target framework is silent rather than offered an uncompilable fix. Only fires when the guard is an `if` whose condition is exactly `x is null` or `x == null` (with the same operator-== check SK1010 makes) and whose body is exactly one `throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(x))` with no message argument and no other statement — a guard that also logs, or that throws a derived exception, or that passes a custom message, is a deliberate choice and is left alone.

## Configuration

- `dotnet_diagnostic.SK1020.severity`
